items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to establishing microchipping standards; in relation to the registration of microchips; and in relation to the examination of rescued companion animals
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4570

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to establishing microchipping standards; in relation to the
registration of microchips; and in relation to the examination of
rescued companion animals

 PURPOSE :

This bill standardizes the radio frequency of microchips implanted
into companion animals; requires veterinarians and animal shelters to
use microchip readers capable of reading the standardized frequency;
requires microchip registration; and requires the examination of
rescued companion animals.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the agriculture and markets law by adding two new
sections 111-a and 111-b.

Section two amends the agriculture and markets 356-a.

Section three sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Microchipping is an effective means to reunite lost pets found by
animal control officers or brought to animal shelters or other
entities with their caregivers. Often the size of a grain of rice,
microchips function as small transponders that require a special
scanner to retrieve the pet owner's contact information. According to
a study published by the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical
Association, microchipped dogs were reunited with their caregivers
about 52% of the time, and microchipped cats were reunited with their
caregivers about 39% of the time.

While much of the world has adopted the standard International
Organization for Standardization (ISO) chip frequency of 134.2 kHz, no
national microchip standard exists in the United States. This bill
requires the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets to create and
implement the rules and regulations to standardize microchip
technology, including the chip frequency and chip readers.

Additionally, the bill requires any entity that implants the chip into
the animal to register the microchip. Without the registration,
standardizing microchip frequencies and readers will be ineffective.
The chipping entity must register the chip with a widely available
microchip registration database listed with the American Animal
Hospital Association's Universal Pet Microchip Lookup Tool.

Lastly, the bill requires organizations receiving a rescued, seized,
captured or impounded companion animal to examine the animal within 24
hours of intake for any identifying marks, tags, or microchips thereby
increasing the likelihood of reunification. Ultimately, animal
shelters and veterinary offices across New York will be relieved of
the costs associated with boarding a lost companion animal, while
simultaneously reuniting animals with their caregivers sooner and more
often.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State
 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall become a law.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to establishing microchipping standards; in relation to the registration of microchips; and in relation to the examination of seized animals and animals taken possession of
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4570A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to establishing microchipping standards; in relation to the
registration of microchips; and in relation to the examination of
seized animals and animals taken possession of

 PURPOSE :

This bill requires the standardization of technology used in
microchips implanted into companion animals; requires the examination
of rescued companion animals; and requires such facilities to notify
owners if they are in possession of an animal they believe to be
missing.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the agriculture and markets law by adding two new
sections 111-a and 111-b.

Section two amends the agriculture and markets law by adding a new
section 380.  Section three sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Microchipping is an effective means to reunite lost pets found by
animal control officers or brought to animal shelters or other
entities with their caregivers. Often the size of a grain of rice,
microchips function as small transponders that require a special
scanner to retrieve the pet owner's contact information. According to
a study published by the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical
Association, microchipped dogs were reunited with their caregivers
about 52% of the time, and microchipped cats were reunited with their
caregivers about 39% of the time.

While much of the world has adopted the standard International
Organization for Standardization (ISO) chip frequency of 134.2 kHz, no
national microchip standard exists in the United States. This bill
requires the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets to create and
implement rules and regulations to standardize microchip technology.

Additionally, the bill requires that the registration of microchips
and the information gathered from registration be compliant with the
rules and regulations developed by the Commissioner of Agriculture and
Markets.

Lastly, the bill requires organizations receiving a rescued, seized,
captured or impounded companion animal to examine the animal within 24
hours of intake, unless surrendered by its owner, for any identifying
marks, tags, or microchips. Should they discover an animal that is
thought to be missing or stolen, the impounding organization should
make a reasonable effort to contact the owner.  Ultimately, animal
shelters and veterinary offices across New York State will be relieved
of the costs associated with boarding a lost companion animal, while
simultaneously reuniting animals with their caregivers sooner and more
often.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall become a law.

summary: Directs the commissioner to establish standards regarding microchip technology used for identification of companion animals; requires the veterinarian or organization that implants the microchip to register such microchip with the microchip company; relates to examination of seized animals and animals taken possession of.
title: Relates to standardization of microchip technology used for animal identification; registering microchips; examining rescued companion animals
